abstract: Second heart field (SHF) progenitors give rise to distinct populations of cardiomyocytes (CMs) in developing heart including right ventricular (rv) and atrial (a) CMs, but robust methods to generate these CM types from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) are lacking. Here we differentiated hPSCs to SHF progenitors, rvCMs and aCMs identified by scRNA-seq transcriptome analysis in comparison to FHF-derived left ventricular (lv) CMs. The hPSC-CM single cell transcriptomes overlapped human fetal heart transcriptomes supporting the chamber-specific identity. The rvCMs strongly express the trabecular myocardium marker, NPPA, in contrast to the lvCMs which express HEY2, a compact myocardium marker. Functional studies demonstrated subtly different cardiac action potentials with a more prominent phase 1 repolarization in rvCMs and chamber-specific pharmacological responses. The gene expression pattern and functional properties suggest greater maturity of rvCMs relative to lvCMs. Overall, this study enables scalable access to chamber-specific hPSC-CMs for disease modeling and potential therapeutic applications.
